en: Now begins the forty-sixth chapter, consisting of ten sections.
O Great Sage, you are omniscient; O you who are compassionate toward the distressed, please tell me in truth how many kinds of states (daśās) there are. || 1 ||
Well asked by you, O Brahmin, who acts for the benefit of the world!
I shall describe before you the tenfold divisions in their many varieties.
Among those various types of *daśās*, the *viṃśottarī* is considered the principal;
by some it is called the *aṣṭottarī*, and by others the *ṣoḍaśottarī*.
O Brahmin, the period (daśā) of twelve years plus one, as well as that of five years plus one, likewise the period of one hundred years, and similarly that of eighty-four years. || 4 ||
Seventy-two years, sixty years, and thirty-six years—these are said by the ancient masters to be the durations based on the lunar mansions (nakṣatras). || 5 ||
Now, the Kāladaśā and the Cakradaśā have been proclaimed by the lords of sages;
furthermore, this Kālacakradaśā is to be honored above all other daśās.
O twice-born one, there are ten *caraparyāya* periods and the period known as *sthira*;
furthermore, the *kendrādya* period should be understood as arising from the planets that act as *kārakas*. (7)
The period (daśā) based on the asterisms occupied by the planets starting with Jupiter (brahma) has been described by some;
likewise, the period known as Māṇḍūkī and the Sthūladaśā are recorded.
O Brahmin, the yoga-ardha-daśā follows, and after that the dṛg-daśā;
then the one known as the trikoṇa-daśā, and likewise the rāśi-daśā is remembered. || 9 ||
O Brahmin, the five types of periods (daśās) to be known are the Yoginī period, the Paiṇḍī period, as well as the Aṃśī period, and likewise the Naisargika period. (10)

The eight-fold division (aṣṭavarga), the ten-fold junctions (daśasandhyā), and that known as the ten-fold maturations (pācakadaśā)—these, along with others such as the Tārā-daśā and so forth, are not considered by all to be [valid] divisions of the zodiacal signs (svargāḥ). || 11 ||
Starting from Kṛttikā and revolving three times, the lords of the decans (daśādhipas) are Ācaṅkura, Āgu, Śabuka, and Keśu, preceded by Vihaga, in successive order.

From the birth asterism up to the asterism occupied by Mars, whatever the number may be, when reduced by multiples of nine, the remainder indicates the lord of the period (daśādhipa); starting from that [asterism], one should calculate the periods.
A full lifespan of one hundred and twenty years was previously declared;
therefore, O best of the twice-born, the Vimshottari Dasha is the primary one in this Kali age.
The periods (daśās) for these [planets] in order are equal to ten; six, ten, horses (7), elephants (8), and moon (1); kings (16), nine moons (19), nine moons (19), mountains (7), and nails (20). (15)
The result for the fear-destroying period is obtained by multiplying the period's duration by the elapsed portion;
from this, the elapsed years and so forth of the period are subtracted from the total duration to find the remaining portion. (16)
O Brahmin, when Rāhu is situated in a quadrant or a trine from the lord of the ascendant, but not in the ascendant itself,
the Aṣṭottarī Dasa should be understood to begin from the Raudrabha constellation.
From that [point], there is a group of four and a group of three; again, a group of four and a group of three.
Thus, one should calculate in due order until reaching one's own birth asterism. (18)
O Brahmin, the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Saturn, Jupiter, Rāhu, and Venus—these planets, excluding Ketu, are to be known as the lords of the periods (daśādhipas). (19)
The years of the periods (daśās) for the Sun and the other planets are five, ten, eight, seven, one, six, twelve, and two respectively. (20)

O best of the twice-born, the duration of the periods for malefic planets is ten years, while for benefics it is indeed one-third; this should be understood as the measure of the period for each individual sign.
Then, one should calculate the elapsed and remaining portions of that [period] just as in the Viṃśottarī system; thereafter, one should declare its results.

If birth occurs during the day in the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇapakṣa) or at night in the bright fortnight (śuklapakṣa), then the aṣṭottarī [mantra] should especially be contemplated for the sake of obtaining results. || 23 ||
When the Moon is in its own horā and the Sun is in the Sun's horā at the ascendant, the "Sixteen-Plus" (ṣoḍaśottarī) yoga should be considered for the sake of knowing the results for men. 24.

Starting from the birth asterism up to the asterism of Puṣya, whatever the number [of asterisms] may be, divided by eight, [the results correspond to] the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Ketu, the Moon, Mercury, and Venus. (25)
Thus, in order, the lords of the periods (daśās) are to be known as the planets excluding Rāhu;
their numbers increase by one starting from eleven, up to eighteen, corresponding respectively to the years. (26)
For one born in the division of Venus, the "twelve-plus" calculation should be considered;
indeed, the count from the birth star up to the star of Puṣan (Revatī) is multiplied by eight. (27)
The Sun, Jupiter, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Saturn, and the Moon—excluding Venus—are the lords of the periods (daśās), lasting for two, three, five, seven, eight, nine, and ten years respectively. (28)
When Cancer is the ascendant at the time of the Sun's entry, the *pañcottarī* is considered [as follows]:
the number of signs from the friend's sign to the birth sign, divided by seven. (29)
In the case of the "remainder of one" (ekādiśeṣa) and so forth, the seventeen lords are to be known in order as:
the Sun, Mercury, Saturn, Mars, Venus, the Moon, and Jupiter. (30)

O twice-born one, excluding Rāhu and Ketu, the twelve [periods] for the seven planets, beginning with the first, should be known as equal in length, increasing by one [month] each in sequence up to Dhṛti.
When the ascendant is in a Vargottama position, the hundred-year Daśā should be considered;
one should calculate from the time of birth until the end of the Pauṣṇa (Revatī) asterism and divide by seven. (32)
The period known as Śatasamā (the hundred-year period) is to be understood from the remaining figure starting from the Sun:
the Sun, Moon, Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn. (33)
O best of the twice-born, these lords of the periods (daśā) are to be known in succession as five, five, ten, ten, twenty, and twenty-five.
When the lord of the tenth house is situated in the tenth house, the eighty-four-year period (caturāśītikā-daśā) is to be known;
the number [of years] from the wind [sign, i.e., Aries] up to the birth sign, divided by seven, [is the duration]. (35)

The remaining ones—Ravi (the Sun), Indu (the Moon), Bhauma (Mars), Jña (Mercury), Guru (Jupiter), Śukra (Venus), and Śanaiścara (Saturn)—are the lords of the periods (daśā) respectively; their durations should be known as twelve years. || 36 ||
One should count from the [natal] sign up to the birth asterism and divide by eight;
from the remainder, the lords of the periods (daśās) are to be known as the eight [planets], beginning with the Sun, in order. (37)
For all those planets that have no retrograde motion, [the period] is nine years;
for one whose lord of the ascendant is in the seventh house, or whose lord of the seventh house is in the ascendant, [the same applies]. (38)
The state (daśā) of that [planet] called the seventy-two-year system is to be considered;
here too, as in the twenty-year system, one should calculate the elapsed and the remaining portions.
When the Sun is situated in the sign of the ascendant, then sixty years are to be considered;
[the sequence is] three from Aśvinī, four, and three again and again. (40)
The periods of Jupiter, the Sun, and Mars each consist of ten years;
thereafter, the periods of Mercury, Venus, Saturn, Rahu, and Ketu each consist of six years. (41)
The number of asterisms from Śravaṇa up to the birth asterism, when divided by eight, leaves as a remainder [one of] the Moon, Sun, Jupiter, Mars, Mercury, Saturn, Venus, or Rāhu. (42)
These are the lords of the ten [periods] in sequence; they are equal, increasing by one starting from one.
When the sun's hour (arkahorā) occurs during the day in the ascendant, and the moon's hour (candrahorā) occurs at night. (43)
The twilight (saṃdhyā) is proclaimed to last for ten nāḍīs—five ghaṭīs before the sun's half-setting and five ghaṭīs after its rising. (44)
The two twilights are proclaimed to consist of twenty nāḍīs;
the twenty ghaṭīs of the day are designated as "full. (45)
The twenty ghaṭikās known as the "deluded" (mugdha) belong to the night;
and that twilight at sunrise, consisting of one and a half nāḍikās, is called the "fragmentary" (khaṇḍa).
At the time of sunset, the twilight known as Sudhā consists of ten nāḍīs;
when the measure of the full mugdha-ghaṭī is doubled, one should divide it by the lunar days (tithis). || 47 ||

Likewise, one should divide the [respective] values for the moon's phases and the Sudhā-ghaṭī by four and by the lunar days (tithis); the result is the measure in years and so forth for the sun and other celestial wanderers.
The measure of the periods (daśā), multiplied by the numbers one and so forth in sequence, and including those joined with Rāhu and Ketu, constitutes the nine known as Kāla. (49)

The wise should determine the sequence of the Cakra periods as follows: at night, from the sign occupied by the ascendant; during the day, from the sign occupied by the lord of the ascendant; and at twilight, from the sign situated in the second house. (50)
O best of the twice-born, the duration of the period for each of the zodiac signs situated in the wheel [of the horoscope] is ten years; this should be understood in due order. 51.
Then, having bowed to Śaṅkara, I shall describe the periods (daśās) of Kālacakra—
those which were previously told with reverence to Pārvatī by the wielder of the Pināka bow.
O best of the twice-born, having extracted its essence for you,
I shall explain how the wise understand the auspicious and inauspicious destinies of human beings.
One should draw a twelve-spoked wheel, with spokes equal in length both horizontally and vertically;
thus, O twice-born one, twelve houses arise, divided into two groups on the right and the left.
In the second and subsequent compartments, one should write the zodiac signs beginning with Aries;
thus is described the Kālacakra consisting of the twelve signs. (55)
The triad beginning with Aśvinī is situated on the left-hand path in the wheel,
and likewise, the triad beginning with Rohiṇī is situated on the right-hand path.
Having thus divided the constellations, one should extract the wheel;
those named Aśvinī, Aditi, Hasta, Kṣema, Mūla, and Proṣṭhapada [are the first]. (57)

One should examine the ten quarters beginning with Aśvinī for the following: Vahni (Kṛttikā), Vāta (Svātī), and so forth, as well as Viśvarkṣa (Uttarabhādrapadā) and Revatī, along with the stars situated to their left.
O Maitreya, I shall now explain clearly how the body and the individual soul are to be perceived within the positions of the stars.
The body and the soul are Aries and Sagittarius;
and for the first quarter of Gemini and the others, the lords of the signs from Aries to Sagittarius are the lords of the periods (daśādhipas).
The pair of deer (Mṛga) are remembered as the body and life-force in the second quarter;
in sequence, up to Gemini (Mithuna), these are the lords of the signs and the lords of the periods (daśās).

O twice-born one, in the third quarter of the ten stars beginning with Dāstra (Śravaṇā), the body is Taurus, the sign is Gemini, Jupiter is the lord, and the [period] measures two, one, seven, one, and nine years. (62)
Kva, Kṣi, Rā, and Markṣa are the lords of the periods (daśādhipati) for the nakṣatras beginning with Aśvinī, respectively, as well as for their fourth quarters. (63)
Cancer and Pisces are the lords of the body and the soul; O best of the twice-born, these nine—the lords of the signs beginning with Cancer—are to be known as the lords of the periods (daśā). (64)
One should contemplate these five constellations—Yama, Ejiya, Citrātōya, Arkṣa, and Āhīrbudhnya—as the stars on the left side of Bharaṇī and the others. (65)

In the first quarter of the southern [hemisphere], the sequence of the body and life-force is the fish (mīna); [the lords of the signs] are eight, seven, six, four, three, two, one, ten, nine, five, three, two, one, and twelve. (66)
In the second quadrant of Yama (the south), the body and the soul reside in the house of the pot (the eighth).
The lords of the houses are [placed] in the directions of Rudra (eleven), Nanda (nine), Candra (one), Akṣi (two), Rāma (three), Abdhi (four), and [the remaining] houses. (67)

The third quarter of Yāmya (Bharaṇī) has Deha and Jīva as its lords; in Tulā and Aṅganā (Vṛścika), the lords of the constellations are seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, eight, and seven respectively. (68)
O twice-born one, when the Sun is in the fourth house of Capricorn, the lords of the lunar mansions are respectively four, five, three, two, one, twelve, eleven, ten, nine, and eight. (69)
O best of the twice-born, one should understand the seventh [wheel] in this manner; I shall now describe the left-hand [method]. One should draw a wheel with twelve spokes as before.
In the second and subsequent compartments, one should write in reverse order starting from Scorpio:
Rohiṇī, Maghā, Viśākhā, and Karṇa—this group of four. (71)
And it has been said by the ancient teachers, O best of the twice-born: "One should observe this [constellation] devoid of planets and stars, like Rohiṇī, as the support for the lunar mansions. (72)
In the asterisms beginning with Rohiṇī, the deities of the body and the life-force are Cancer and Sagittarius;
[the lords of the signs] are nine, ten, eleven, twelve, eleven, three, four, and four. (73)
In the second quarter of the Dhātṛ [Yoga], Deha and Jīva are the two Tulas;
[the others are] Aṅka, Āga, Vasu, Sūrya, Īśa, Diś, Aṅka, Vasu, Jūka, and Pā. (74)
In the third quarter, Brāhma and Dīrghajīva are in the house of the pitcher (Aquarius).
The lords of the signs are six, five, four, three, one, nine, nine, one, nine, eleven, and eleven. (75)
The lords of the signs are remembered as follows: Rohiṇī and Antapada are Cancer and Pisces;
the Sun and Moon are Gemini and Virgo; and [the others] are Taurus, Sagittarius, Capricorn, and Leo respectively. (76)
Cāndra, Raudra, Bhaga, Āryamaṇa, Mitra, Indu, Vasu, and Vāruṇa—
this group of eight stars should be understood by the wise in sequence, following the order of the moon.
O twice-born one, Cancer is the body and Pisces is the soul in the case of the signs beginning with Capricorn;
the lords of the periods (daśādhipas) are the rulers of the signs from Pisces up to Cancer taken in reverse order.

The bull-bodied [Venus] and the Gemini [Mercury] are the lords of the second quarter of Capricorn; the lords of the [twelve] houses are three, two, one, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, ten, one, two, and five. (79)
The body and the soul are in the pair of crocodiles (nakra-yugma) in the third quarter of Mṛga;
the lords of the signs are three, five, four, six, seven, eight, twelve, eleven, and ten respectively. (80)

Aries is the body (deha), Sagittarius is the life-force (jīva), and these are the lords of the periods (daśādhipas) in the fourth quarter of Capricorn; from the reverse order of Sagittarius, these are the rulers of the signs between Aries and the end [of the zodiac]. (81)
Thus, regarding the counter-clockwise group, the states of the body, the vital breath, and so forth were declared by Śambhu to Pārvatī; this has now been told by me here.
O Great Sage, tell me for how many years each of the lords of the decans (daśeśas) presides,
and explain to me the commencement of their periods (daśās), including what has already been experienced and what remains to be experienced.
The periods (daśās) of the Sun and the other [planets] are twenty-one, seven, nine, ten, six, eight, and four [years], respectively, according to their being the lords of the zodiac signs. (84)
Whether at the time of a man’s birth or at the time of a query, whichever is the [lord of the] Navāṃśa, the years of those nine signs starting from that [lord] are said to be his lifespan. (85)
At the beginning, one's lifespan is complete; in the middle of the division (aṃśa), it is half;
and at the end of the division, others—wise men—say there is supreme suffering. (86)
Having thus understood this clear established doctrine, the wise man should calculate the degrees of the zodiacal signs;
hereafter, I shall explain the method for that by means of proportion.
The elapsed *tārās* divided by three, with the remainder multiplied by four and increased by the current *pada*, shall be the degrees (*aṃśaka*) of the zodiacal signs. (88)
In Aries, one hundred; in Taurus, eight times ten (eighty); in Gemini, three times eight (twenty-four) years;
in Cancer, they are said to be six times eight (forty-eight), and the same number applies to its two trines.

The years of one's own life are multiplied by the degrees of that [ascendant] in which the person was born, calculated from the elapsed nadīs, palas, and so forth, and then divided by fifty-five (55). || 90 ||
In this manner, the commencement of the great periods (mahā-daśās) occurs according to the sequence of the divisions (aṃśas);
one should count up to nine, and that [number] is proclaimed as the respective lifespan.
Then, the duration of its own year is multiplied by the elapsed ghaṭīs and so forth of the sign; this is divided by four times the [total] revolution of the signs.
The result is the elapsed portion, and the remaining portion is obtained by subtracting that from the total duration.

The degrees, minutes, and seconds traversed by the Moon’s digits, multiplied by the measure of its own year and divided by two hundred, should be known by the wise as the elapsed years, days, and so forth; from that, the remaining portion (bhogya) is to be determined.

In the *savya* [clockwise] method, that which is the first part is called the body (*deha*), and the final part is designated as the individual soul (*jīva*); in the *apasavya* [counter-clockwise] method, it is the reverse.
One should count the body and so forth on the right side, and the life-force and so forth on the left;
having understood this, the astrologer should then predict its results. (95)
The movement of Kālacakra has been declared by the ancient seers to be threefold:
one is called the "frog-like" movement, and the other is known as the "monkey-like" movement. (96)
The third is proclaimed as the "Lion’s Gaze" (siṃhāvalokana);
the wise declare the act of moving by leaping to be the "Frog" (maṇḍūka). || 97 ||
Moving backward is known as the "monkey" (markaṭī), and likewise, movement from the arrow (vāṇa) up to nine [steps] is the "lion's glance" (siṃhāvalokana). 98.
The movement between Virgo and Cancer, and between Leo and Gemini, is called the frog's gait (maṇḍūkī-gati).
Likewise, the movement between Cancer and Leo is described as the monkey's gait (markaṭī-gati). || 99 ||
The movement of Rāhu occurs between Pisces and Scorpio, and between Sagittarius and Aries;
having reflected thus, one should understand the results of the Kālacakra Dasa. 100.
Indeed, during the period of Maṇḍūka-gati, there is danger from kinsmen on the left side, or danger arising for one's parents from poison, weapons, fire, fever, thieves, and the like. (101)
If two frogs appear on a lion, one should predict the mother's death;
or else there will be one's own death, fear of the king, or the danger of *sannipāta* (a complex fever).
If one walks to the left while passing a female monkey, there will be loss of wealth, grain, and cattle;
there may be the death of a father, laziness, or even the death of those equal to him. (103)
If the lion’s glance is on the left, men will experience fear of wild animals, the destruction of friendship and affection, and suffering caused by people of equal status. (104)
There may also be falling into wells and the like, danger arising from poison, weapons, or fire;
or falling from a vehicle, affliction by fever, and the destruction of one's dwelling. (105)
In the Maṇḍūka-gamana [flight], if it occurs on the left, the wise one should predict affliction for women, sons, and others, as well as fever, fear of wild beasts, and loss of position.
In the case of the Markaṭī gait, one should predict fear of water, loss of position,
the death of the father, royal wrath, and wandering through difficult forests.

In the Siṃhāvalokana [configuration], there is a loss of position on the left side and the death of one's father; or else, one should consider the result to be a death equal to that [of the father]. (108)
When Scorpio has passed from Pisces, fever certainly occurs;
when Cancer has passed from Virgo, there is the destruction of brothers and kinsmen. (109)
When the Sun has entered Gemini from Leo, disease will certainly befall women;
and when it has entered Cancer from Leo, there is death for embodied beings. (110)
One should know that the death of a paternal relative occurs when [the Sun] enters Aries;
furthermore, if it is joined by malefic planets there is fear, but if joined by benefic planets there is auspiciousness.

Whether auspicious or inauspicious, the results of the Dasa of the Kalachakra are determined from the portion of the directions occupied by the zodiac sign, or from the asterism moving in the directions starting with the East.

O best of the twice-born, at the time of that planet's period (daśā), the effects for all men should be declared according to the direction it occupies and following the path of the traditional instructions.
When Cancer has moved from Virgo, there will be great fruit in the eastern region;
taking recourse to the northern country, the journey will be auspicious. (114)
When the Sun has entered Gemini from Leo, one should avoid the eastern quarter;
even at the conclusion of an undertaking, there will be a successful journey toward the southwest.
When the sun has moved from Cancer into Leo, there is loss of undertakings in the south;
having resorted to the southern direction, there will be a return toward the west.
When the sun has moved from Pisces to Scorpio, there arises a difficulty;
when it moves from Sagittarius to Capricorn, a difficulty certainly arises. (117)

O best of the twice-born, when the sun is in Aries during a journey, there may be illness, captivity, or death; however, when it is in Scorpio, there is happiness, prosperity, and the acquisition of a wife.
When the sun has moved from Leo into Cancer, one should avoid the western direction;
in an auspicious conjunction, one should declare an auspicious result, but in an inauspicious one, an inauspicious result.
In the portion of Aries, one becomes a hero or a thief; in the portion of Taurus, one is possessed of fortune;
in the portion of Gemini, one becomes wise; and in the portion of Cancer, one becomes a king. (120)
In the Leo portion, one is honored by kings; in the Virgo portion, one becomes a scholar;
in the Libra portion, one would be a king’s minister; and in the Scorpio portion, one is destitute. (121)
In the Sagittarius portion he is endowed with knowledge; in the Capricorn portion he is a doer of evil;
in the Aquarius portion he is engaged in the business of trade; and in the Pisces portion he possesses wealth and grain. (122)
If the body or the soul is conjoined with the Sun, Mars, Saturn, or Rāhu, death shall occur in each single conjunction; what then need be said when there is a conjunction of many? (123)
If the ascendant is joined with malefic planets, there will be disease; if Jupiter is joined [with them], there is great fear.
From both [malefics and Jupiter] together, mental anguish and disease shall arise, and through the paths of untimely death, one may perish.

When one meets death with four [planets], while the body and the soul are joined by inauspicious ones, and both the body and the soul are simultaneously conjoined with malefic planets, then [this occurs]. (125)
There will be fear of kings, thieves, and the like, as well as death; of this there is no doubt.
When the Sun is [the lord of the day], danger from fire is to be known, and when the Moon is waning, there is fear of water. (126)

In the case of Mars, there is suffering caused by weapons; in the case of Mercury, there will be affliction from wind-related disorders; in the case of Saturn, one should know there is suffering from abdominal tumors (gulma); and in the case of Rāhu or Ketu, there is fear of poison.
If Mercury, Jupiter, or Venus enters the house of the body or the house of the soul, they all bestow happiness and prosperity and destroy disease and sorrow. (128)

When conjoined with mixed houses, one shall obtain mixed results. During the period of a malefic sign, both the body and the life-force are distressed; during the period of an auspicious sign, it is certain that what is auspicious occurs. (129)

The Dasa of an auspicious planet in an inauspicious house is said to yield mixed results; likewise, the Dasa of an auspicious planet conjoined with a malefic in an auspicious house yields mixed results. (130)
At the time of the Cakra-dasha of that sign which was situated in the first house at the time of a person's birth, there is health of the body and great happiness. (131)
In an auspicious [sign], there is full happiness; in a malefic [sign], the occurrence of diseases and so forth in the body.
When the planets are situated in their exaltations and other such positions, there is the attainment of kingdom, honor, and wealth. (132)
When the planetary period (daśā) of the sign situated in the second house occurs, then there is excellent food, sons, happiness from women, and the acquisition of wealth. || 133 ||

The acquisition of knowledge, eloquence of speech, and the passing of time in excellent conversation—such shall be the fruit when the asterism is auspicious; if it is a malefic asterism, the result is otherwise.
When the Kālacakra Dasa of the third house is in operation, then there is happiness from brothers, valor, fortitude, and also great pleasure. (135)
The acquisition of golden ornaments and garments, and honor in the royal assembly—such shall be the fruit in an auspicious asterism; in a malefic asterism, the result is otherwise.
When the Dasa of Kalachakra falls for a planet situated in the state of happiness (Sukhabhava), then there is happiness from kinsmen and the attainment of land, houses, and royal power. || 137 ||

Good health, the acquisition of wealth, and happiness derived from clothing and vehicles—these are to be known as auspicious when the asterism is favorable; if it is a malefic asterism, the result is otherwise.

When the Dasa of Kalachakra falls for one who has reached the asterism of the son (Purva-phalguni), there is the attainment of happiness from sons, wife, and sovereignty, as well as health and association with friends. || 139 ||
Knowledge, intellect, fame, gain, fortitude, and the rise of valor—these are fully auspicious when in a benefic sign; in a malefic sign, the result is otherwise.
When the Kālacakra daśā of a sign that has entered the state of an enemy occurs, then there is great fear from thieves, kings, fire, poison, and weapons. (141)

There is also the possibility of diseases such as urinary disorders (prameha), abdominal tumors (gulma), and anemia (pāṇḍu); such shall be the result in an inauspicious asterism, whereas in a auspicious asterism, one should indicate mixed results. (142)

When the Dasa of Kalachakra occurs for a sign that has entered the state of being the wife (the seventh house), then there is the taking of a hand in marriage, as well as happiness such as the acquisition of a wife and sons. (143)
The acquisition of agriculture, weaponry, and clothing, honor from the king, and great fame—these are the full fruits when the sign is auspicious, and half of that when it is malefic. (144)
Then, the Kālacakra Dasa of the asterism situated in the eighth house (the house of death) brings about the loss of position, great suffering, the loss of kinsmen, and the depletion of wealth. (145)
One should indicate poverty, fear of food and disease, and danger from enemies;
the result is full in a malefic sign and half that in a benefic sign. (146)
When the Kālacakra period of Dharmabhāvagatarkṣa occurs, one should predict happiness regarding children, wife, wealth, agriculture, and the home. (147)

The successful accomplishment of virtuous deeds and Dharma, as well as the acceptance by great people, occurs when there is a full auspiciousness in the heap of merit, and half of that in the heap of demerit. (148)

When the Kālacakra period of the asterism occupied by the sign of the karma-bhāva occurs, there is the attainment of sovereignty, honor from the king, and happiness arising from children, wife, and so forth. (149)
Sovereignty is the fruit of virtuous deeds; the passing of time in the company of the righteous is the fruit of a meritorious zodiacal sign (rāśi), while in a sinful sign, the fruit is mixed. 150.
When the Kālacakra Dasa of the asterism situated in the ninth house occurs, there is the attainment of happiness from sons, wife, and kinsmen, favor from the king, and great pleasure. (151)
The acquisition of wealth and clothing, good health, and association with the virtuous arise;
the fruit is complete when the sign is auspicious, but it is diminished when the sign is malefic. (152)
Then, the Kālacakra Dasa of the sign situated in the twelfth house brings about the failure of one's efforts, laziness, bodily affliction, and loss of position. (153)
One should declare poverty, the fruitlessness of actions, and likewise useless expenditure as the results in a malefic sign; in a benefic sign, the result is half of that.
I shall now describe the *caradaśā* (mobile periods) of the signs from the ascendant (*lagna*) up to the twelfth house (*vyaya*).
Therefore, those learned in this matter know the duration of the period to be the number of signs from that [starting point] up to its own lord. 155.

The *pada* should be known by means of the three signs starting from Aries; in the case of an odd *pada*, the calculation for determining the years of the *daśā* proceeds in regular order, whereas in the case of an even *pada*, it proceeds in reverse order. (156)
O twice-born one, Venus and Mars are remembered as the two lords of Scorpio;
Saturn and Rāhu are proclaimed to be the two lords of Aquarius. (157)
Now, O Brahmin, the determination regarding these two fields with dual lords is being made: if both lords are situated in their own respective signs, they are indeed joined together. (158)
If one does not consider [the planets] beginning with the Moon there for twelve years, then if one [planet] is in its own sign and the other is situated elsewhere, [the result follows]. (159)
Then, one should take the Lord situated elsewhere and lead him to the [relevant] state;
if both are in other asterisms, whichever of those two is stronger [should be taken]. || 160 ||
From that very [position], O twice-born one, the *daśās* (periods) are to be taken either in direct or reverse order;
in this consideration of strength, a planet with a planetary period (*sagraha*) is stronger than one without.
If both of those [planets] possess their own planets and are strong, then the one with the superior planet [is stronger];
when the planetary conjunctions are equal, strength is to be known from the strength of the zodiacal sign (rāśi). || 162 ||
The movable, fixed, and dual signs are to be known as possessing strength in their respective order;
when there is equality between the sign and the planetary nature, that which has many years becomes strong. (163)
If one [planet] is situated in its own exaltation and the other is located elsewhere, one should indeed take the sign occupied by the planet in its exaltation, setting aside the other. || 164 ||
In the case of a superior planet, one should add one year;
likewise, in the case of an inferior planet, one should subtract one year. (165)
Having thus examined everything, one should declare the results of the birth horoscope.

Whether in direct or reverse order, according to the sequence of the states of the signs, the wise man should calculate the moving periods (caradaśā), beginning from the sign of the ascendant. || 167 ||
Now, O twice-born one, I shall fully explain the period known as Sthira-dasha:
seven years are prescribed for a movable sign, eight for a fixed sign, and nine for a dual sign. || 168 ||
Because the periods of the ten planets are stable, this is called the "Stable" (Sthira) period; this period revolves starting from the asterism occupied by the planet of Brahma (the Sun). 169.
"O Sage, how is that which is called the 'grasping of Brahman' (brahmagraha) to be known?
If you have compassion for me, please explain this more clearly. (170)

Among the lords of the sixth, eighth, and twelfth houses, whichever one is strong and situated in an odd-sign (viṣamarāśi) shall become Brahmā; he stands behind the strong lord of the ascendant and the lord of the wife. 171.

If the lord of the eighth house from the Karaka, or even Jupiter (Brahmā), is situated in the eighth house; or if Saturn is in the eighth house and Jupiter is its sixth lord; or if Jupiter is the lord of the sixth house from that [Saturn]—[in these cases, there is no longevity]. || 172 ||
Many [planets] may possess the characteristics [of being a Brahma-khecara]; among them, the one with the greater number of degrees should be recognized as such.
If there is equality of degrees, the one with the greater strength is to be known as the Brahma-khecara. (173)
The duration of the period is equal to half the sum of the two [ascendants], and this period proceeds starting from the ascendant, the seventh house, and the vital breath (prāṇa). (174)

Whichever sign is stronger between the ascendant and the seventh house, from that [sign], one should proceed according to the order of strength of the signs situated in the quadrants and other houses. || 175 ||

Indeed, for the zodiacal signs and the planets as well, the years of their periods (daśās) should be understood in this very same way as those of the movable signs; and the nature of the planets should also be known accordingly. (176)
One should count from the lord of the sign occupied by the Karaka up to both limits;
the number of years for the Karaka’s Dasha is whichever of these two figures is greater. (177)

Beginning from the self as the agent (ātmakāraka), the period known as the *kāraka-daśā* proceeds in sequence; they know the duration of this period here to be the number of signs from the ascendant up to the *kāraka*. (178)

O twice-born one, the period known as Trikūṭa, which is another synonym for Maṇḍūka, occurs between the ascendant and the seventh house; whichever sign among these two is stronger [determines it]. (179)
Then, in due order, it should be brought [to the next] in odd signs, and likewise in reverse order in even signs;
and the periods (daśās) of the three peaks (trikūṭas) are to be understood as equal, like those of the fixed signs.
For the purpose of investigating the departure [from the world], some maintain that the *cūlā-daśā* should be considered;
whichever of the two—the eighth house from the ascendant or the seventh house—is stronger, [that one is taken]. (181)

O Brahmin, in the case of an odd sign, those ten years begin from that [sign] in direct order, and in an even sign, in reverse order; death occurs there in the sign of Bala or Māraka, as in the case of a fixed sign.

Whichever sign is the strongest among the trikonas (trines) of the birth ascendant, from that [sign] the wise man should calculate the period (daśā), following the sequence of movable signs (cararāśi). 183.
The trilateral [period] is to be grasped in forward and reverse order when the [number of] periods is odd or even;
this is called the trilateral period (trikoṇākhyadaśā), which is equal and ends with its own lord. (184)

From the ascendant, one should calculate the periods (daśās) of the ninth house and the signs aspected by it; then, from that [ascendant], one should again calculate the periods of the tenth house and the signs aspected by it. 185.

The years for the signs seen by the eleventh house are equal to those of the fixed [signs]; because this aspect proceeds according to the power of the aspect, it is therefore known as the "aspect-decade" (dṛg-daśā). || 186 ||
In the case of a movable sign, the signs suitable for observation should be taken in direct order; in a fixed sign, in reverse order.
In the case of a dual sign, they are in direct order for odd-numbered signs and in reverse order for even-numbered signs.

The periods (daśās) of the signs beginning with the ascendant within a lunar mansion (ṛkṣa) are known as the "sign periods" (rāśidaśā). The elapsed portion [of the mansion] multiplied by twelve and divided by the duration of the mansion's passage (bhabhoga) yields the result. (188)
The [period] beginning with the sign and so forth should be added to the sign of the ascendant and so forth, reduced by twelve;
starting from that, the periods (daśā) are to be known in direct order when the number is odd, and in reverse order when it is even. 189.
The ten-year period, multiplied by the elapsed portion and divided by thirty, yields the result;
this should be understood as the elapsed time in years and so forth, while the remaining (bhogya) portion is obtained by subtracting it from the total duration. || 190 ||
First, one should arrange the five vowels beginning with *a* in their proper order;
then, one should write the consonants from *ka* to *ha*, excluding *ṅa*, *ña*, and *ṇa*, beneath the vowels. (191)
In the horizontal row-order, according to the division of five by five, the letters ṅa, ña, and ṇa are not mentioned; they do not exist at the beginning of names.
If these [vowels] occur, then they should be known as *gajaḍa* respectively;
in whichever vowel the first letter of one's own name occurs, that vowel and the others [following it] are [to be understood]. (193)

The lords of the five periods (daśās) are respectively twelve years each; the sub-periods (antardaśās) and so forth within those periods should be understood according to the sequence of the vowels. 194.
O twice-born one, the planetary periods known as Varṇadā were previously described by me;
now the Yoginī periods, as taught by Śambhu, are being told.
Maṅgalā, Piṅgalā, Dhanyā, Bhrāmarī, Bhadrikā, as well as Ulkā, Siddhā, and Saṃkaṭā—these are proclaimed as the eight Yoginīs. || 196 ||
From Maṅgalā was born Candra, from Piṅgalā the Sun (Divākara), from Dhanyā was born the one worshipped by the gods (Bṛhaspati), and from Bhrāmarī was born Kuja. || 197 ||
From Bharḍika was born Budha, and from Ulkā was born Śanaiścara; from Siddhā was born Bhārgava, and from Saṃkaṭā Tama arose. (198)
One should add three to the birth asterism and divide by eight;
in the remainder of one and so forth, the Yoginīs beginning with Maṅgalā are to be known. (199)
The ten equal periods (daśās) of these [planets] should be known to increase successively by one, starting from one;
one should calculate the elapsed and remaining portions by means of the [planetary] longitude and its movement through the asterisms.

For those planets for whom a lifespan has been declared as being derived from the *piṇḍa*, the *bhāga*, or the *nisarga*, their periods (*daśā*) should be understood as the *paiṇḍī*, the *āṃśī*, and the *nisargajā* respectively. (201)

The first period belongs to whichever among the Ascendant, the Sun, and the Moon is strongest; thereafter, the periods of those situated in the angles (kendras) and other houses are to be understood according to their relative strength. (202)
One should consider their results by means of the strength of the eightfold division (aṣṭavarga);
these are called the periods of the eightfold division (aṣṭavargadaśā) by the ancient masters. (203)

The twelfth part of the maximum lifespan is proclaimed as its *sandhyā* (dawn/dusk period); the *sandhyā-daśā* of the ascendant and the other [houses] is recorded as being of that same measure, in due order. (204)

The *sandhyā* should be made by taking the qualities of the *rasas* and dividing them by the moon and fire (three); the result should be placed in the first square, and half of that should be distributed among the next three. (205)
Having assigned one-third [of the total] to the eight squares, one should declare their results;
in this manner, one should determine the "cooking" [planets] for the twelve houses. (206)
In this context, the duration of the *tārā-daśā* is recorded by some as twenty-one years;
the stars [are situated] in locations such as the bow, the arrow, the club, and the head. (207)

From a strong planet situated in a quadrant (kendrastha), there arise the states of self, wealth, misfortune, security, enemy, achiever, and death; as well as friendliness and supreme friendliness. (208)
O Brahmin, the period (daśā) of Tārā should be known as bestowing fruits equal to her name; that planet which is situated in the quadrant (kendraka) is said to possess this period. (209)
Thus, O Brahmin, these ten types of divisions have been told to you in manifold ways;
hereafter, I shall describe the sub-divisions of these antardaśās.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the periods (daśā-phala), etc., [Chapter] 47.
O Sage, I have heard of the many varieties of these ten [vows] in various ways;
please tell me out of compassion what their respective fruits are.
The fruit of the ten planets is twofold—common and specific—arising from their inherent nature and from the influence of their positions. II.2.
The results during the planetary periods (daśās) should be understood according to the strength of the planets;
one should declare the results at the commencement of a period based on the planet situated in the first decanate (dreṣkāṇa). || 3 ||
When a planet is situated in the middle decanate of a period, its results should be declared for the middle of that period;
when it is in the final decanate, the results are for the end; and these effects are reversed if the planet is retrograde.

When the lord of the dasa begins the dasa and is situated in the ascendant, conjoined with or aspected by a benefic, or is in its exaltation, its own sign, or its own friendly sign, the results of that dasa will be auspicious. || 5 ||

If [a planet] is situated in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is positioned in its sign of debilitation, its fall, or an enemy's sign, its result is inauspicious; now I shall describe the results for all planetary periods (daśās).

When [a planet] is in its Mūlatrikoṇa, its own sign, its own exaltation, or its highest exaltation; or when it is situated in a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house, and is conjoined with the lords of the ninth or tenth houses; || 7 ||
When the Sun is endowed with strength and joined with the strengths of its own vargas, during that period there is great happiness, auspicious gains such as wealth, and so forth. (8)
There is exceedingly auspicious royal honor, horse-rides, and so forth;
and when conjoined with the lord of the fifth house, one obtains the birth of a son.
In connection with Dhaneśa (Venus), one should predict sovereignty over elephants;
in connection with Vāhanādhipa (Saturn), it brings the acquisition of three vehicles.
During the period of the strong Sun, there is the favor of the king, abundance of wealth, the position of commander-in-chief, happiness for the man, and the acquisition of clothing and vehicles. (11)
If [the lord of the ascendant] is in the sixth or eighth house below, weak, conjoined with malefic planets, associated with Rāhu or Ketu, and joined with the lord of an inauspicious house; || 12 ||
In that year, there will be great suffering caused by the destruction of wealth and grain;
there will be royal displeasure, exile, punishment from the king, and the loss of wealth. (13)
Affliction by fever, loss of reputation, and conflict with kinsmen and friends;
fear of the destruction of ancestors and indeed inauspiciousness within the home. (14)
One experiences mental anguish and hatred toward one's paternal kin;
if the Sun is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic, there is some happiness in the middle of that period. A wise astrologer should declare evil results if it is aspected by a malefic house.
Thus, O Brahmin, the results of the Sun have been briefly declared by me;
now, according to the Viṃśottarī system, I shall state the results of the Moon's period (daśā).
When [the Moon] is in its own exaltation or its own sign, situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, conjoined with a benefic planet, and endowed with full strength; || 17 ||
When joined with the lords of karma and bhāgya, and endowed with the strength of the lord of the vehicle,
it brings about the acquisition of sovereignty, good fortune, wealth, grain, and other such things at the beginning and the end.
In the house [of this asterism], auspicious undertakings, vehicles, and audiences with the king will occur;
there shall be success in efforts for one's goals, as the house has received the side-glance of Lakṣmī.

By the influence of the Mitra lord, one shall obtain good fortune, the acquisition of a kingdom, great happiness, the gain of horses, swings, and the like, as well as white garments and other such items.

When the Moon is situated in the house of wealth (the second house), whether in its exaltation or in its own sign, there is satisfaction from obtaining a son and other blessings, and an abundance of houses, cattle, and wealth.
One obtains the acquisition of manifold wealth, an increase in fortune, great happiness, the recovery of deposits, honor from the king, and the attainment of knowledge. (22)
If [the Moon] is in its sign of debilitation (nīca) or waning, there will be loss of wealth;
if it is in Aquarius (duścikya) and endowed with strength, there will be happiness in some respects and wealth in others.
If [the Moon] is weak and conjoined with malefic planets, there will be physical lethargy,
mental anguish, suffering for servants, loss of wealth, and injury caused by those belonging to the mother’s side of the family.

If the Moon is weak and conjoined with malefic planets in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, there will be enmity with the king, mental distress, and the destruction of wealth, grain, and other possessions. (25)

When the Moon is in an unfavorable position but endowed with strength, it brings distress to the mother, mental anguish, physical lethargy, and mental pain; yet it may also bring some gain or happiness, and sometimes even physical lethargy. In such a case, one should predict auspicious results through pacificatory rites. || 26 ||

In this manner, I shall describe the auspicious and inauspicious results of the planetary periods (daśās) for a Mars situated in its own sign, an exaltation, or the like, as well as in a debilitation or an enemy's sign. || 27 ||
When Mars has reached its highest point, is in its exaltation, its Mūlatrikoṇa, its own sign, or in a quadrant, a trine, the eleventh, or the second house; || 28 ||

When [the lord of the ascendant] is endowed with full strength, aspected by benefics, and situated in a benefic Navamsha, it brings about the acquisition of a kingdom, the gain of land, and the attainment of wealth, grain, and so forth. (29)
One shall obtain preeminence, honor from the king, vehicles, garments, and ornaments; furthermore, one will find a secure position in a foreign land and experience happiness with one's siblings. (30)
When Mars is always situated in the tenth house, being endowed with strength in the second or seventh house, there shall be gain of wealth through valor and victory over enemies in battle. (31)
One attains happiness at the beginning of the period (daśā) regarding wife, children, wealth, and even honor from the king; however, one should predict suffering at the end of the period.
When Mars is situated in a malefic house such as the eighth, is devoid of strength, conjoined with malefics, or aspected by malefics, that period brings about undesirable results. (33)

In this same manner, O delight of the twice-born, I shall describe the houses and other factors for Rāhu and Ketu before you, for the purpose of knowing the results of their planetary periods (daśās).
For Rāhu, Taurus is known as the exaltation; for Ketu, Scorpio is the exaltation.
These should be understood as their Mūlatrikoṇas (primary trines), followed by Gemini and Sagittarius respectively.
Some authorities declare that Aquarius and Capricorn are houses, as are Virgo and Pisces;
in their periods (dāyas), there is great happiness and abundance of wealth, grain, and other riches.
The acquisition of a vehicle as desired through the influence of friends or one's lord, the birth of a son, the construction of a new house, reflection on dharma, and a great festival. (37)

There will be honor from foreign kings, as well as clothing, ornaments, and decorations, when [the Moon] is joined with benefics, aspected by benefics, and conjoined with a yoga-producing planet. || 38 ||
If the Kendra, Trikona, or Lagna is in a Dvishchakra sign occupied by a benefic planet, it brings all prosperity and happiness through the favor of the great king. (39)
If Rāhu is in the eighth or the twelfth house, one should predict suffering during its period (dāya), despite the honor shown by the Yavana ruler and the occurrence of auspicious events at home.
If there is an association with a malefic planet, or conjunction with a house of death, or if [the lord] has entered its sign of debilitation, there will be loss of position and mental anguish. (41)
There shall be the loss of wife and sons, the eating of contemptible food, bodily affliction at the beginning of the Dasha, and the depletion of wealth and grain. (42)
During the middle of the period, there shall be happiness; in one's own country, it brings gain of wealth.
At the end of the period, one encounters hardship, loss of position, and mental anguish. (43)
I shall now describe the results of the periods of that [planet] who is honored by the lords of the gods, and who is considered by the wise to be exceedingly auspicious in all undertakings. (44)
When Jupiter is in its exaltation or its own sign, situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine;
or in its Mūlatrikoṇa, the eleventh house, its exaltation degree, or its own Navāṃśa. || 45 ||
The attainment of a kingdom, great manliness, renown for royal honor, being endowed with elephants and horses, and the worship of gods and Brahmins. || 46 ||
There shall be happiness from wife, sons, and so forth, as well as the acquisition of vehicles and garments;
there will be success in rites such as sacrifices, and the hearing of Vedānta and other [scriptural studies]. (47)

Through the favor of the Great King, there shall be the attainment of desired goals bringing happiness, the acquisition of palanquins and other such luxuries, auspiciousness, and great well-being. 48.
There is the gain of children, wife, and so forth, and the giving of food is greatly pleasing;
yet, when Jupiter is joined with malefics in the seventh house and conjoined with the Sun in the twelfth or eighth house, [these results do not come to pass].
One shall experience displacement from one's position, mental anguish, suffering for one's children, great fear, loss of livestock and wealth, and undertake pilgrimages and similar journeys. (50)
In the beginning, it yields results that are indeed difficult, yet it brings the gain of four-footed creatures;
in the middle and at the end, one attains happiness, royal honor, and prosperity.
Now, I shall describe the results of the planetary periods (daśā) of that son of the Sun who is proclaimed to be the most inferior among all the planets. || 52 ||
If Saturn is in its exaltation, in its own sign, or in a friendly sign;
or if it is in its Mūlatrikoṇa, in the ninth house (bhāgya), in its exaltation degree, or even in its own Navāṃśa; || 53 ||
If Duścikya is in the eleventh house, there will be honor and prosperity from the king, good reputation, gain of wealth, and the pleasure of engaging in scholarly debate. (54)
By the grace of the great king, one should perform the Rājayoga characterized by elephants as vehicles and ornaments; this brings great happiness from the commander of the army.
The marks of Lakṣmī’s sidelong glance bring about the attainment of sovereignty;
they produce auspicious prosperity in the home and the gain of a wife, sons, and so forth. (56)
If Saturn is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is debilitated, or even set, there will be suffering from poison, weapons, and the like, loss of position, and great fear. (57)
Separation from father and mother, suffering caused by wife and children, royal injustices, and likewise imprisonment—these are the undesirable [consequences]. (58)

When Saturn is conjoined with or aspected by a benefic, or is associated with a Yogakāraka [planet], or when Saturn is in Pisces or Sagittarius occupying a quadrant, a trine, or the eleventh house; || 59 ||
The attainment of a kingdom with great energy, abounding in elephants, horses, and garments. || 60 ||
Now, I shall describe the results of the periods (daśās) of that prince who is celebrated among all the [planetary] lords, the son of Tāreśa. || 61 ||

When a benefic planet is in its exaltation, in its own sign, or situated in a quadrant, the eleventh house, or a trine, and is associated with a friend's sign, there is great happiness during its period (dāya). 62.
There shall be the acquisition of wealth, grain, and the like, as well as good reputation, riches, and prosperity;
an abundance of knowledge, the favor of the king, and the increase of virtuous deeds and qualities. (63)
One obtains happiness from children, wife, and others, as well as physical health, great pleasure, the enjoyment of milk-based meals, and wealth from one's business endeavors. (64)
When a benefic planet joined with auspicious aspects is in the ninth or tenth house, its period is powerful in its lordship and yields full results at the outset. (65)
If [the lord of the ascendant] is joined with or aspected by malefic planets, one shall incur enmity with the king, mental anguish, opposition from kinsmen, and travel to foreign lands. || 66 ||
If Mercury is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, there will be service to others, quarrels, great fear from physical ailments, and the loss of profit, enjoyment, and wealth.
One should predict affliction by wind, loss of wealth, and jaundice;
as well as fear of kings, thieves, and fire, and the destruction of agriculture, cattle, and land. (68)
At the beginning of the period, there is wealth, grain, acquisition of knowledge, and great happiness;
there is prosperity through the well-being of one's sons, and it brings gain of riches on the virtuous path. (69)
In the middle there will be honor from the king, but at the end there will be suffering. || 70 ||
I shall now describe to you the results of the periods (daśā) of that Ketu which is called Kabandha by the wise, situated between the planets Rāhu and Tamas. || 71 ||

If [the planet] is in the tenth house, the eleventh house, a trine, or a benefic sign, aspected by benefics, or in its own exaltation or a benefic division, there will be pleasing favor from the king. (72)
One should predict sovereignty over a country or a village, the acquisition of vehicles, the birth of a son, and travel to foreign lands; these bring about happiness. (73)

In the period (dāya) of Ketu, when it is in the sign of Aries (duścikya), or in the sixth or eleventh house, it bestows happiness consisting of the pleasure of children and wife, as well as the acquisition of four-footed animals. (74)
He exercises sovereignty over a portion of his friends, accompanied by elephants and horses;
yet, within the period (daśā) of the Daśadaurājayoga, there is great fear. (75)
There is wandering to distant lands and likewise physical exhaustion when Ketu is in the second, eighth, or twelfth house,
and is aspected by or conjoined with malefic planets.
It brings about shackles, the loss of kinsmen, displacement from one's position, mental anguish, gains through association with Śūdras and the like, and a state crowded with diseases. || 77 ||
Now, O Brahmin, I shall describe the results of the periods (daśās) of that preceptor of the Daityas, who dwells within all beings in the form of semen (śukra). 78.
When Venus has reached its highest point, being in its exaltation, its own sign, or a quadrant, there is the attainment of royal consecration, as well as vehicles, garments, and ornaments. (79)
There shall be the constant acquisition of elephants, horses, and cattle, the enjoyment of sweet foods,
and the majesty of royal honor from a sovereign lord of an unbroken mandala.
The sound of drum-like musical instruments resounds in the house, brought about by the glance of Lakṣmī;
when that [planet] is situated in its own Trikoṇa, there is sovereignty, wealth, houses, and riches. (81)
It brings about marriage festivities, the prosperity resulting from the welfare of one's sons, the command of an army, and the reunion with beloved kinsmen. 82.

If Venus is in the sixth, eighth, or twelfth house, or is debilitated, or situated in the house of expenditure (the twelfth), there will be the recovery of lost kingdom and wealth, as well as the accumulation of cattle and assets in the home.
It causes hatred toward oneself and one's kinsmen, suffering for one's wife and family, the loss of the fruits of one's endeavors, and the destruction of cattle, buffaloes, and other livestock. (84)

Or there may be suffering caused by one's wife, children, and so forth, or separation from oneself and one's kinsmen, due to the predominance of destiny and karma when [the Moon] is situated in the sign of the ascendant or the vehicle-sign. (85)
During that period, there is great happiness, the status of a ruler over a country or village, and engagement in meritorious deeds such as the construction of temples and tanks. (86)
Through the gift of food, there is great happiness and the constant enjoyment of sweet meals;
as well as enthusiasm, fame, prosperity, and the abundance of wife, sons, and wealth.
In this manner, the fruit will manifest during its own period; other strengths [operate] during the periods of others.
However, if the lord of the second house is deficient, there will be affliction of the body.
To avoid that fault, one should mutter the Rudra or the Tryambaka hymn;
one should give a white cow or a buffalo as a gift, and from that, health shall arise.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the periods (daśās) of the specific lunar mansions (viśeṣanakṣatra). || 48 ||
The ancient masters have thus declared the results based on the positions and states [of the planets];
now I shall describe the results arising from the mutual relationships between the lords of the houses. (1)
During the period of the lord of the ascendant, there is good fame and physical happiness;
however, during the period of the lord of the second house, there is either distress or fear of death.
During the period of the lord of the Sahaja house, the results of evil should be known for men;
however, during the period of the lord of the house of happiness (Sukha), there shall be happiness from home and land.
During the ripening period (pāka) of the fifth lord, there is the attainment of knowledge and happiness from sons;
during the time of the lord of the sixth house's period, there is bodily affliction and fear of enemies. || 4 ||
During the ripening period (pāka) of the lord of the seventh house, there is suffering for one's wife and fear of death;
during the time of the major period (daśā) of the lord of the eighth house, there is fear of death and loss of wealth.
During the period of the tenth house (Dharma), there is abundant gain, fame, and happiness;
during the period of the lord of the tenth house, there is honor in the assembly of kings.
During the period (daśā) of the lord of the eleventh house, there is obstruction regarding gains and fear of disease;
O twice-born one, the period of the lord of the twelfth house bestows much suffering upon men.
At the commencement of a period (daśā), even for one situated in an auspicious house, the result is auspicious;
likewise, for one situated in an inauspicious house, even if [the planet] is auspicious, the result is not favorable.
The Dasa of the lord of the tenth house when conjoined with the lord of the fifth house is auspicious;
when conjoined with the lord of the ninth house, it is exceedingly auspicious. (9)
The period of even a planet conjoined with the lord of the fifth house is auspicious; likewise, the period of one conjoined with the lord of the ninth house is most excellent. (10)
The period of the lord of the ninth house is auspicious even when associated with the lord of the fourth house;
likewise, the period of the lord of the tenth house is auspicious even when situated in the fifth house. || 11 ||
Thus, the periods of the lords of the trines situated in the angles are auspicious;
likewise, the periods of the lords of the angles situated in the trines are also auspicious. (12)

If the lord of a quadrant (kendrēśa) is situated in an angle (koṇabhāva) and the lord of an angle (koṇēśa) is situated in a quadrant, those learned in the science of astrology declare the daśās of both to be auspicious. || 13 ||
Even the lords of the sixth and eighth houses, when conjoined with the lord of a trine (koṇa), have their periods declared to be auspicious by those expert in time. (14)

If the lord of a trine (koṇa) is situated in a quadrant (kendra), or if the lord of a quadrant is situated in a trine, then for the planet conjoined with either of these two, or aspected by them— || 15 ||

The wise astrologers declare that such a period bestows auspicious results, provided the lord of the ascendant is situated in the ninth house and the lord of the ninth house is situated in the ascendant. (16)
During the period of these two, however, there arises the manifestation of pleasant qualities;
the lord of the tenth house is situated in the ascendant sign, and the lord of the ascendant has gone to the tenth house. (17)

During the ripening of the periods (daśā) of those two, the acquisition of a kingdom will certainly occur; this also applies when they are situated in the third, sixth, or eleventh houses, or are conjoined with the lords of the third, sixth, or eleventh houses. (18)
Even for auspicious planets, their periods yield malefic results if they occupy positions of death (māraka-sthāna) or are conjoined with the lords of such death-positions. (19)
Furthermore, the periods (daśās) of planets situated in the eighth house yield undesirable results;
thus, the results of the periods should be inferred from their relationship with the lord of the house. 20.
Now begins the chapter on the results of the Kālacakra periods (daśā). 49.
Now, O best of Brahmins, I shall describe the results of the periods (daśā) of Kālacakra;
therein, first, I shall state the results of the lords of the zodiac signs, beginning with the Sun. (1)
One should declare diseases such as hemorrhaging and biliousness for men when [the Sun] is in Arka;
the Moon bestows wealth, fame, increase of progeny, clothing, and ornaments. (2)
Mars likewise quickly brings about bilious fever, as well as glandular swellings and eruptions;
Mercury shall always bestow an increase of progeny and wealth. (3)
Wealth, fame, increase of progeny, and various enjoyments are the results of Bṛhaspati; while the results of Bhṛgu are proficiency in knowledge, marriage, a home, and grain. || 4 ||
Excessive heat, great suffering, and the loss of kinsmen are the results of Saturn.
In this manner, one should declare the results of the planetary periods (daśās) according to their association with the signs starting from Aries. || 5 ||
In Aries there is suffering from blood disorders, but in Taurus there is an increase in grain;
in Gemini there is the attainment of knowledge, and in Cancer one becomes a lord of wealth.
In the solar asterism (Sūryakṣa), there is affliction from enemies and the loss of daughters and wives;
in Tālikā, one attains the status of a royal minister; and in Vṛścika, death shall occur.
There shall be gain of wealth in Sagittarius in the ninth decanate of Aries; in Capricorn, there are evil deeds; and in Aquarius, there is trade alone. (8)
In Pisces there is the accomplishment of all goals; in Scorpio there is fear from fire; in Libra one is honored by kings; and in Virgo there is an increase of enemies.

In the Navāṃśa of Cancer, there is distress regarding one's wife; in Leo, it causes skin diseases and eye ailments; and in the Navāṃśa of Taurus within Gemini, there will be obstruction to one's livelihood.
In Taurus, there is the gain of wealth; in Aries, however, it causes fever and disease;
in Pisces, there is affection for one's maternal uncle; and in Aquarius, there is the increase of enemies. (11)
In Capricorn there is distress for the thief; in Sagittarius, an increase of weapons;
in Aries, a clash of arms; and in Taurus, there will be strife. (12)
In Gemini one attains happiness, in the Navāṃśaka of Gemini likewise;
in Cancer there is the onset of distress, and in Leo it causes royal displeasure. (13)
In Virgo, there is honor from one's brothers; in Libra, a man does what is pleasing [to others];
in Scorpio, there may be affliction to the ancestors; and in Sagittarius, there is the arising of knowledge and wealth. || 14 ||
In the Capricorn Navāṃśa there will be fear of water; in Aquarius, an increase in grain;
and in Pisces, the attainment of happiness and prosperity within the Cancer Navāṃśa. (15)
In Scorpio there is distress and pain; in Libra, indeed, the result is excessive; in Virgo, there is great gain; and in Cancer, there is affliction from wild beasts. (16)
In Leo, there is the gain of a son; in Gemini, the increase of enemies;
in Taurus, the acquisition of quadrupeds; in the Aries portion, fear from animals;
and in the ninth division of Leo, there shall be a long journey during the period of Pisces.
In Aquarius there is the gain of wealth; in Capricorn it brings the acquisition of property;
in Sagittarius there is association with brothers; and in Aries there is the increase of one's mother.
In Taurus, there shall be an increase of sons; in Gemini, an increase of enemies;
in Cancer, affection for women; and in Leo, an increase of disease. (19)
In the ninth division of Virgo, there shall be an increase of sons;
in Libra, the gain of wealth; and in Scorpio, the increase of brothers.
In Sagittarius there is happiness from one's father; in Capricorn, conflict with one's mother;
in Aquarius, gain of sons and wealth; and in Pisces, conflict with enemies. (21)
In Aries there is conflict with one's wife; in Libra, obstruction by water;
in Virgo, there shall be an increase of wealth; and in the ninth division of Libra— || 22 ||
In Cancer there is indeed loss of wealth; in Leo, opposition from the king;
in Gemini, gain of land; and in Taurus, it brings about the acquisition of wealth. (23)
In Aries there will be fear of snakes and the like; in Pisces, likewise, fear from water;
in Aquarius, gain from business; and in Capricorn, fear of illness. (24)
In the Navāṃśaka of Sagittarius, there shall be gain of wealth;
in that of Scorpio, there shall be gain of wealth; in Aries, there shall be gain of wealth; and in Taurus, there is an increase of land. || 25 ||
In Gemini there shall be all success; in Cancer it brings about all success;
in Leo there shall be prior prosperity; and in Virgo there will be strife. (26)
In Libra there will be gain of wealth; in Scorpio one shall incur disease;
and in Sagittarius, as well as in its ninth-part (navāṃśaka), there will be an increase of sons.
In Capricorn there shall be the gain of a son; in Aquarius, an increase of grain;
in Pisces, one attains auspiciousness; and in Scorpio, one is afflicted by poison.
In Libra there is gain of wealth; in Virgo, an increase of enemies;
in Cancer, one obtains a wife; but in Leo, one is afflicted by wild beasts. (29)
In Gemini there is injury to trees; in the ninth division of Capricorn, there is gain of wealth;
in Taurus, however, there is gain of wealth; but in Aries, it causes eye disease. (30)
In Pisces there shall be a long journey; in Aquarius, the increase of wealth;
in Capricorn, the attainment of all success; and in Sagittarius, the increase of enemies. (31)
In Aries there is the destruction of happiness, and in Taurus death occurs;
in Gemini one attains auspiciousness during the ninth division of Aquarius.
In Cancer there shall be an increase of wealth; in Leo, however, there is honor from the king;
in Virgo there is the gain of wealth, and in Libra one shall obtain profit.
In Scorpio one encounters fever; in Sagittarius, an increase in enemies;
in Capricorn, conflict with one's wife; and in Aquarius, opposition regarding water.

In the Pisces [ascendant], however, there is total auspiciousness; having understood the results according to the sequence of the nine and ten divisions of Pisces, one should declare all the fruits. || 35 ||
During the period (daśā) of malefic planets, a wise person should perform propitiatory rites (śānti).
Whatever has been stated regarding royal yogas and so forth, and whatever results have been declared in the chapter on designations (saṃjñādhyāya), [should be applied here].
A wise person should indeed apply all of that with a keen intellect at the appropriate time;
thus has the result of the Kālacakra periods been briefly declared. (37)
Now begins the chapter on the results of the periods (daśās) starting from the Carakadaśā. || 50 ||
O twice-born one, regarding those periods (daśās) previously mentioned as having names such as Cara, Sthira, and so forth— I shall now describe their auspicious and inauspicious fruits before you.
In proclaiming the results of the twelve houses beginning with the ascendant, one should apply the strength of the respective lords of those signs as appropriate. (2)
When the lord of the sign is endowed with strength, its fruit is then full;
if it has middling strength, the fruit is middling; and if it is devoid of strength, the opposite occurs. || 3 ||
O Brahmin, whichever sign bestows a period (daśā), if its eighth house or trine is conjoined with a malefic planet, that period brings suffering.
If a malefic planet is situated in the third or sixth house, it is proclaimed as the "Jyādi" (bow-string) yoga; however, if that position is joined by a benefic planet, defeat occurs instead. || 5 ||
O twice-born one, when a benefic or even a malefic planet is situated in the eleventh house, gain is certain;
this is especially so when the sign that bestows the period (daśā) is conjoined with a benefic planet.
Indeed, the auspicious results of the Dasa of that sign should be understood to occur when it is in a benefic house;
however, if it is joined with malefics in a benefic house, there is first auspiciousness followed by inauspiciousness.
If a malefic planet is conjoined with a benefic, there is happiness first and then misfortune;
if it is in a malefic sign and conjoined with a malefic, that period (daśā) bestows suffering at all times.
O twice-born one, when a sign associated with an auspicious field is joined by both malefic and benefic planets, [it is a Śubhakṣetra-daśā].
First there is hardship, but afterwards happiness arises without doubt;
in an auspicious asterism (nakṣatra) a favorable result is to be declared, whereas in a malefic asterism the fruit is inauspicious.
In the second, fifth, or ninth house, there will certainly be royal favor and victory;
however, if a malefic planet occupies those positions, the results of that period should be known as inauspicious.
In the fourth house, however, there is auspiciousness and happiness; in the eighth house, if it is auspicious, there is health;
and in the ninth house, if it is auspicious, there is an increase in dharma and happiness from one's elders.
In the case of a contrary [result], there is perversion; in the case of a mixed [result], a mixture is proclaimed.
When the ripening and the enjoyment are abundant with evil, there is physical affliction and mental anguish. (13)
In the seventh house, suffering regarding wife is declared due to both ripening karma and current experience when there is a malefic;
in the fourth house, there shall be loss of position, and in the fifth, affliction to children.
In the tenth house there will be loss of fame, and in the ninth house there will be affliction to the father;
when the malefic has reached the eleventh house through its transit, all suffering becomes non-obstructive.
When a benefic planet is situated in the aforementioned places, one should predict happiness;
when a benefic planet is situated in a quadrant (kendrasthāna), there is gain that brings victory over enemies. (16)

Having examined the positions of the planets at the time of birth, as well as their aspects and their placement in their respective signs, one should declare the results pertaining to each of those signs.
If a sign is beautiful in appearance and auspicious planets are situated behind it, its period (daśā) is said to bestow auspicious results; in the opposite case, the reverse occurs.
When benefics and malefics are situated in the trine,
the eighth, or the twelfth houses, the auspicious or inauspicious results should always be declared by the astrologer during their respective periods.
The afflictions of the zodiac signs of Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn are said to be, respectively, Scorpio, Leo, Taurus, and Aquarius. (20)
If a malefic planet is situated in the eighth house, the house of obstacles, or in the sign occupied by the lord of the eighth house,
there will be great sorrow, imprisonment, calamities, and disease.
If that planet is in its exaltation or its own sign, there will be auspiciousness, happiness, and the arrival of wealth;
if it is devoid of those, there will be unhappiness, and its period (daśā) will not yield results.
If Bādhaka is situated in the sixth or eighth house and conjoined with Rāhu, there is great fear;
during a journey, one encounters imprisonment, oppression by the king, and danger from enemies. (23)
If the Sun, Mars, Rāhu, and Saturn are situated in the sign of the Moon's transit,
there will be a downfall during that transit and great fear from the king's wrath.
If a debilitated planet is situated in the ascendant, the third, or a trine, or if it is conjoined with a debilitated malefic in that same sign, one should predict fear of death. || 25 ||

When a planet is situated in its own exaltation or a trine within the house of fruition (bhukti-rāśi), and the period of that planet's fruition (bhukti-daśā) is attained, then a person shall obtain happiness. || 26 ||
He attains the status of lord of cities and villages, the birth of a son, the arrival of wealth, auspiciousness, abundant fortune, and the highly exalted position of commander-in-chief. (27)

If the lord of the ninth house is aspected by Jupiter and situated in a benefic sign, there will be the acquisition of wealth, auspiciousness, and the birth of a son during its period (daśā). || 28 ||
The pairs of signs beginning with Cancer (Sitā) and Capricorn (Asita) are the enemy signs of the Sun;
Aquarius, Libra, and Scorpio are the enemy signs of the Moon; and Aries, Leo, and Aquarius are the enemy signs of Mars. || 29 ||
Aquarius, Pisces, Capricorn, Libra, and Virgo are the signs following Gemini; thereafter, Cancer, Pisces, Scorpio, and Aquarius are recorded as the enemy signs. (30)
Taurus, Libra, Aries, and Virgo are the inimical signs for Jupiter; and Leo, Scorpio, Cancer, and Sagittarius are the inimical signs for Venus. (31)
O twice-born one, the wise man should consider Aries, Leo, Sagittarius, Scorpio, and Cancer to be the enemies of Saturn; in this manner, he should contemplate the periods of other planets.

Those planets which bestow royal yoga, as well as those that are auspiciously situated in the middle houses, or from whichever [house] they occupy the second, third, or fourth, are givers of auspicious results. (33)
One should declare the auspiciousness of those [planets] during their periods, arising from royal yogas and the like;
even a malefic situated between two benefics is considered to bestow auspicious results. (34)
The auspicious period of a benefic planet has entered the midst of its own favorable sub-period;
since it is situated in a trine from a benefic, its period also bestows auspicious results. (35)
If the result from the commencement to the end of the auspicious sign of a friend is favorable,
one should divide it by each sign in this manner for the year and so forth, and declare that result.
If the commencement [of the period] occurs in that trine, or in a benefic house, or in a benefic sign, or begins with a benefic, the dasa will be exceedingly auspicious. (37)

If a malefic planet is in a sign beginning with a benefic [sign], it is considered auspicious at the commencement of its period (daśā); if it begins auspiciously, how can it be otherwise? One should declare the fruit according to the nature of the commencement. (38)

O twice-born one, if at the commencement or during a mass of evil [periods] the lord is weak, or if it is in its sign of debilitation and so forth, or at the end of its period and so forth, one should predict a reversal of fortune.

Wherever a planet situated in its sign of debilitation, or in a trine thereof, or likewise when the lord of that sign is in debilitation, there exists a connection with planets in their states of debilitation. (40)
O best of the twice-born, it indeed causes the reversal of fortune, as well as the loss of wealth, grain, and other possessions, and likewise fear of disease within the body. (41)

For Rāhu and Ketu, the four signs beginning with Aquarius and the four beginning with Scorpio are their own signs; an undertaking begun therein during their respective periods will be auspicious. (42)

If one should declare a period to be auspicious while it is situated in the house of death (Māraka), or if that period is aspected by or conjoined with [malefics] in the sign where its end occurs; 43.
There may be loss of wealth due to royal displeasure through Venus or Mercury;
this occurs if the end of the period falls in an enemy sign, or if it is conjoined with or aspected by Rāhu.
O best of the twice-born, this result is not to be considered during the ripening (pāka) of Saturn;
nor is this result to be considered when Saturn is in the sign of Capricorn (nakra-rāśi) as the provider of the period (daśā). || 45 ||
At the end of Rāhu’s period, there is the loss of all possessions, death, or imprisonment;
or there may be exile from one's place, or one experiences great suffering. (46)
If a malefic planet is situated in that trine, one should certainly predict suffering;
thus, a wise man should definitively declare all matters, whether auspicious or inauspicious. (47)
If the sign occupied by Rāhu and others should be the giver of the period (daśā), then at that time as well, what was previously stated must be carefully considered. (48)
If the commencement or the end of a period falls upon a malefic planet, it is not auspicious;
