and if Rāhu is in that very same place, there will be imprisonment and the destruction of wealth. (49)
If Rāhu is in any house at the commencement of the Dasa, destruction is indicated;
there is the loss of one's home, and if Rāhu is in the second house, it causes suffering regarding wealth. (50)
If the Moon and Venus are in the twelfth house, there will certainly be royal wrath;
if Mars and Ketu are there, there will be death by fire and great suffering.
O Brahmin, if Jupiter and Venus bestow a kingdom in the second house at the commencement or the end of their periods, this is the result for that which is situated in the second house. (52)
Thus has the result of the states of the *argalas* been demonstrated by the wise;
for whichever planet, whether malefic or benefic, should reside in an auspicious *argala*. (53)
Therefore, when the ascendant is aspected by its ruler, it is rendered strong, provided that a planet aspects it and does not stand in a reverse *argala* position. (54)
But during the period (daśā) of that state, the result will be the opposite;
even when there is a good aspect, O best of the twice-born, one should declare it to be auspicious without hesitation.
In whichever house there is a connection with a benefic lord or a planet in its exaltation, during the period (daśā) of that house, one shall attain uninterrupted and ultimate sovereignty. (56)
If the lord of a house occupies or aspects its own sign of exaltation,
there will be very great gain of wealth at the time of that house's period.
Because [the lords] have gone to the twelfth house, there is loss of wealth during that period;
because malefic planets occupy the trines, there is the destruction of one's own welfare therein.
There will be loss of sons, suffering for the father, and great mental anguish,
because the lords of the trines, the eighth house, and the twelfth house are Saturn, Mars, and the son of the Sun (Rāhu).
In that conjunction of Ketu and Rahu, there is suffering for one's children, loss of wealth,
wandering in foreign lands, distress, and fear at every step.

Therefore, if malefic planets, debilitated planets, and the like are situated in the sixth or eighth houses, there will be constant and most unbearable suffering from disease, enemies, and the king. (61)
Since the fourth house is cruel, it causes the destruction of houses and fields;
there is loss of livestock, and in that case, if Mars is present, there is a fire in the home caused by negligence.
If Saturn [is unfavorable], there will be pain in the heart; if the Sun, provocation by the king;
if Rāhu, the seizure of all one's possessions and fear arising from poison, thieves, and the like. (63)
Because Rāhu is in the tenth house, there will be travel to holy pilgrimage sites; because the auspicious planets are situated in the tenth, first, and ninth signs from the ascendant. (64)

Knowledge, wealth, dharma, virtuous deeds, fame, prowess, and success—these are attained from [the Sun] when it has reached its exaltation or is associated with benefic planets, even though it is the enemy of the fifth house (Venus). 65.
The attainment of children, wife, and so forth, as well as great honor from kings, occurs because the lords of the ninth, tenth, and ascendant signs are situated there for the sake of the son. (66)

The accomplishment of each respective purpose shall come to pass through the pursuit of yoga for one's welfare, in whichever [house] Jupiter, Venus, or the lord of auspicious planets is situated. (67)

There is auspiciousness and all-round prosperity, with the satisfaction of gods and Brahmins, when the exaltation signs (tuṅgakheṭas) are in the fourth house, or when there is a benefic lord or a planet [there]. (68)
There will be the acquisition of vehicles and villages, and a great increase in livestock; if the Moon is there, there will be gain consisting of much grain and liquids. (69)
When the moon is full, he shall obtain a treasure or acquire a collection of jewels;
there, under the influence of Venus, he will be honored by the playing of lutes, drums, and other musical instruments, as well as by songs.

If Jupiter is situated in the ninth house (bhāgya), there will certainly be the attainment of a golden swing (āndolikā), provided it is in its exaltation and joined with auspicious planets by aspect or conjunction with the lords of the ascendant, the tenth house, and the ninth house. || 71 ||
One should contemplate the fruit that arises from the bestowal of each respective state as being the great result, such as supreme excellence, great sovereignty, and imperial dominion. (72)
Each individual planetary period, being divided by its own eighteen-fold qualities,
indeed produces a ripening of results that is endowed with variety.
When a planet is in its highest exaltation (paramocca), or merely in its exaltation (tuṅga), or even slightly below or above that point;
or when it is in its Mūlatrikoṇa sign, its own sign (svakṣetra), or the sign of its own or a very friendly planet (svādhimitragraha); || 74 ||

Likewise, [the results are neutral] when the Moon is in the house of a friend at that time, or in the house of a neutral planet, or in the house of an enemy, or in a sign situated above the point of debilitation. (75)
Therefore, within the limit of the sign of depression (nīca), at the end of the depression sign, in the highest degree (paramāṃśaka),
in the division of the enemy or depression signs, in its own varga accompanied by a khala, and in a quadrant or trine— 76.
For a planet that is situated [in its own house], afflicted in battle,
or severely oppressed, the result of its own qualities is the diminution of its period.
For one who has attained the highest excellence and is endowed with great vigor, the period known as Sampūrṇā bestows sovereignty, prosperity, and auspiciousness. 78.
She grants a long-term residence for those marked by the side-glances of Lakṣmī, as well as for those who have attained great height and those who possess superior prowess. (79)
The aspect known as *pūrṇā* bestows abundant sovereignty, yet it also brings about affliction, even for a planet that has fallen into an extremely low state and is weak. (80)
But when empty, it yields undesirable results, bringing disease, misfortune, and death;
whether situated in an excessively high or an excessively low position, it is called *avarohiṇī* when it is in the middle.
Indeed, for a planet that has reached its sign of exaltation, the period known as "the middle" (madhya) bestows wealth;
this applies to a planet situated in the middle of the six signs between the end of its fall and the end of its exaltation. (82)

Furthermore, the *daśā* of a planet situated in its sign of exaltation, its own sign, or its friendly sign is called *Ārohiṇī*; however, that of one situated in its sign of debilitation, an enemy's sign, or its *navāṃśa* is named *Adhamā*, which increases fear, affliction, disease, and suffering. (83)

These periods yield results corresponding to their names at the time of fruition, depending on the relationship with the lord of the ninth house and Jupiter, as well as through yogas, aspects, kendras, and other such factors. (84)

One should also infer the commencement of fortune from the inheritances of others—specifically those whose horoscopes yield results or which bestow auspicious planetary configurations (bhāgya-yoga). || 85 ||
Beyond Vakrimā, he shall also [conquer] other sky-dwellers who are weak and incapable of bestowing fruits through sacrifice; thus it shall be fruitful.

These states, which are well-connected through their relative gradations, bestow results according to the established rule of full, half, and quarter [strength] for those planets occupying their own signs, exaltations, and so forth. (87)

Planets situated in signs that rise by their head (śīrṣodaya) or by their crotch (bhaga) bestow their own results at the beginning of their respective periods; those situated in signs that rise by both [head and crotch] bestow middling results during their periods. || 88 ||

Planets situated in the sign of their *pṛṣṭhodaya* (ascendant by descent) bestow their results at the end of their own periods; likewise, they are naturally auspicious during the time of seizing friends. 89.
Then, one should calculate the suffering for those who fall into its opposite;
starting from the sign and the lord of the tenth house, it extends through twelve signs. (90)
Having divided [the total] by the twelve signs, one should calculate the periods (daśā) and sub-periods (bhukti);
therein, for each individual sign, that which goes to its friend's or its own house [is to be considered].
In that [ascendant], one should predict auspicious results preceded by the attainment of sovereignty and other such riches;
provided, however, that it is not conjoined with malefics situated in difficult houses, in the house of an enemy, or with debilitated or cruel planets.
In that [year], due to the abundance and deficiency of the *bindu* (dot) in one's own group of eight, there will be meaningless quarrels, disease, fear of death, and so forth. (93)

One should understand the increase and decrease of that house from its own domicile through the addition of houses [to the ascendant] in due order; thus one knows the auspiciousness or inauspiciousness of children, wives, and so forth. (94)

And due to the divisions of the elements and so forth, as well as the conjunctions of the planets with the elements and so forth; and due to the distinctions of auspicious and inauspicious aspects, even when joined with both auspicious and inauspicious [planets]. (95)
One should deduce the distinctions in results from the differences between favorable and unfavorable positions;
in this same manner, one should determine the respective sub-periods (antardaśās) for all the planets as well. (96)
Having calculated the transit through the signs starting from one's own sign, one should declare the results;
having thus divided one's own internal sub-period (antar-daśā) again and again. 97.
The End of India
